evidence.explanation: The study links reduced NADPH to glutathione-dependent redox defense in the brain and neurodevelopmental delay.

hypotheses/0.description: Biallelic TKT variants reduce transketolase activity in the non-oxidative branch of the pentose phosphate pathway. The resulting block causes accumulation of polyols (erythritol, arabitol, ribitol) and pentose(-ulose) phosphates and is proposed to reduce NADPH available for nucleic acid synthesis, cell division, and maintenance of cerebral glutathione, thereby explaining growth failure (short stature) and neurodevelopmental delay.

evidence.snippet: APOC2 was upregulated in TNBC tissues and was negatively correlated with M1 macrophage infiltration.
evidence.explanation: Establishes APOC2 upregulation in TNBC as negatively correlating with anti-tumor M1 macrophage infiltration. This is the tissue-expression arm of the study, stated before any cell-line or xenograft work.

evidence.snippet: KLHL1 promoted APOC2 protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby enhancing M1 macrophage polarization and suppressing the malignant behavior of tumor cells.
evidence.explanation: KLHL1-mediated APOC2 degradation enhances M1 macrophage polarization, restoring anti-tumor immunity. The quoted mechanism follows the co-immunoprecipitation and 4T1 cell experiments, so it is cell-based.

evidence.snippet: in vivo xenograft experiments demonstrated that APOC2 reduced M1 macrophage polarization and increased tumor weight and volume, whereas KLHL1 overexpression counteracted the oncogenic effects of APOC2
evidence.explanation: Confirms the APOC2-driven suppression of M1 polarization, and its reversal by KLHL1, in a tumor-bearing animal rather than in culture.

steps/0.description: The TNBC microenvironment is immunosuppressive, with pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization suppressed. Apolipoprotein C-II (APOC2) is upregulated in TNBC tissue and inversely correlates with M1 macrophage infiltration; overexpressing it in tumor cells suppresses M1 polarization and promotes tumor growth, so the effect on macrophages is tumor-cell-extrinsic. KLHL1 (a Cullin3-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase substrate adaptor) degrades APOC2 via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and reverses this immunosuppressive phenotype by restoring M1 polarization.

evidence.snippet: analysis of human datasets (TCGA-BRCA and Kim cohorts) revealed that tumor necrosis factor superfamily member 9 (TNFSF9) and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand (CXCL9) expressions correlate with improved prognosis and enhanced immune cell infiltration
evidence.explanation: Human breast-cancer cohorts tie CXCL9 expression to immune infiltration and outcome. Graded INDIRECT because a positive correlation between higher CXCL9 and better infiltration is the claim read backwards; it establishes the axis, not that low CXCL9 is what excludes the T cells.

evidence.snippet: targets the protein triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) expressed by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
evidence.explanation: Establishes TREM2 as a surface marker of the tumor-associated macrophages this node binds, which is what the CL:4047053 binding asserts. The quoted sentence states the premise the paper's targeting strategy rests on, not a result it produced, so quote_role is BACKGROUND. The paper's own experiments are murine, but this sentence reports no experiment at all, which is why evidence_source is OTHER rather than MODEL_ORGANISM.

steps/1.description: CXCL9 is the dominant CXCR3 ligand recruiting cytotoxic T lymphocytes into solid tumors, and tumor-associated macrophages are a principal source of it. Where the macrophage compartment is immunosuppressed, intratumoral CXCL9 is low, and in breast cancer its expression tracks with both immune infiltration and survival. Restoring it is sufficient to pull CTLs back into the tumor, which is what makes the deficiency causal rather than merely correlated.

evidence.snippet: Due to limited tumor immune infiltration in TNBC, the effectiveness of immunotherapy is constrained
evidence.explanation: States the node for TNBC specifically, and the consequence that makes it matter clinically. quote_role BACKGROUND records that the sentence is the paper's framing rather than a result it reports, and evidence_source is OTHER because the sentence itself reports no study.

evidence.snippet: codelivery of a Toll-like receptor agonist and CXCL9-encoding mRNA encapsulated in our Ab-LNP successfully ameliorates immunosuppression and improves tumor infiltration and activity of CTLs
evidence.explanation: A therapeutic rescue cited as validation of the mechanism it targets: restoring CXCL9 to TREM2-positive macrophages improves CTL infiltration, so the exclusion is CXCL9-dependent and reversible. INDIRECT because the claim follows from the intervention working rather than being asserted, and the system is an orthotopic mouse model.

steps/2.description: TNBC tumors are poorly infiltrated by CD8-positive cytotoxic T lymphocytes, which is the proximate reason immune checkpoint blockade benefits only a minority of patients: a drug that releases a brake on T cells does little where the T cells are not present. Supplying CXCL9 reverses the exclusion in model systems.

evidence.snippet: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by the lack of estrogen and progesterone receptor expression and lacks HER2 overexpression or gene amplification.
evidence.explanation: This review abstract defines TNBC by absent ER and PR expression with absent HER2 overexpression, directly supporting loss of hormone receptor signaling as a defining mechanistic feature.

steps/3.description: TNBC lacks expression of estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) and progesterone receptor (PGR), eliminating the growth-promoting effects of estrogen signaling that drive most breast cancers. This absence removes a key therapeutic target but also indicates fundamentally different tumor biology.

steps/4.description: In the absence of hormone receptor signaling, TNBC is driven by alternative oncogenic pathways including EGFR signaling, PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Many TNBCs have TP53 mutations eliminating this tumor suppressor checkpoint.

evidence.snippet: PARP inhibition causes synthetic lethality in breast cancers associated with germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations and is routinely used in clinical practice for metastatic breast cancer.
evidence.explanation: Supports the therapeutic consequence of homologous-recombination deficiency in BRCA-mutated breast cancer. It does not support the "~20% of TNBC" prevalence figure in the node description, which remains uncited.

steps/5.description: A significant subset of TNBC (~20%) harbors germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations resulting in homologous recombination deficiency. This creates sensitivity to platinum chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality.

evidence.snippet: TP53 gene is mutated in approximately 80% of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).
evidence.explanation: Supports near-universal loss of the TP53 checkpoint in TNBC, the principal permissive lesion for the mutator/chromosomal-instability phenotype. Direct TNBC genomic-scarring evidence is still needed.

steps/6.description: Loss of high-fidelity double-strand-break repair, compounded by near-universal TP53 inactivation, produces a mutator phenotype and pervasive chromosomal instability. This is the enabling characteristic that supplies the driver lesions feeding the alternative oncogenic pathways and aggressive behavior of TNBC.

evidence.snippet: It accounts for 10-15% of incident breast cancers and carries the worst prognosis.
evidence.explanation: Abstract states TNBC carries the worst prognosis, supporting aggressive behavior.

steps/7.description: TNBC is characterized by high proliferation rates, early metastasis (especially to viscera and brain), and shorter time to recurrence compared to other breast cancer subtypes. The aggressive biology reflects activation of multiple oncogenic pathways and loss of tumor suppressors.

edges/0.description: Other signaling pathways drive proliferation in absence of ER

edges/1.description: Multiple activated pathways drive aggressive phenotype

edges/2.description: DNA repair defects lead to mutation accumulation

edges/3.description: Accumulated driver lesions and chromosomal instability fuel clonal evolution and the aggressive clinical course.

evidence.snippet: in vivo xenograft experiments demonstrated that APOC2 reduced M1 macrophage polarization and increased tumor weight and volume, whereas KLHL1 overexpression counteracted the oncogenic effects of APOC2
evidence.explanation: Evidences the edge rather than either node it joins: the same manipulation that reduces M1 polarization increases tumor weight and volume, and reversing it reverses both.

edges/4.description: Suppression of M1 polarization promotes tumor progression.

evidence.snippet: Myeloid-restricted ALDH2 ablation converts TAMs from a pro-tumorigenic phenotype to immunostimulatory regulators, concomitantly amplifying CD8+ T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity to improve ICB responsiveness
evidence.explanation: Reversing the macrophage immunosuppressive phenotype restores the CXCL9 output and the CD8 infiltration that depends on it, which is this edge read in the rescue direction.

edges/5.description: Macrophages are a principal source of the CD8-recruiting chemokine CXCL9, so an immunosuppressed macrophage compartment leaves the tumor short of it.

evidence.snippet: Subsequent CXCL9 derepression in TAMs facilitates persistent CD8+ T cell infiltration and enhances their cytotoxic effector functions
evidence.explanation: States the edge itself: relieving the block on macrophage CXCL9 is what produces CD8 infiltration, so the deficiency is what withholds it.

edges/6.description: Too little CXCL9 in the tumor means too little CXCR3-driven chemotaxis of CD8-positive T cells across the tumor margin.

evidence.snippet: effectively suppresses TNBC growth by reprogramming the intra-tumoral immune landscape
evidence.explanation: Reversing the infiltration deficit suppresses tumor growth, which is this edge read in the rescue direction. INDIRECT because the growth effect is attributed to the immune landscape as a whole rather than to CD8 infiltration in isolation.

edges/7.description: Without cytotoxic T cells in the tumor, immune control of outgrowth is lost.

evidence.snippet: TP53 gene is mutated in approximately 80% of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).
evidence.explanation: Abstract reports TP53 mutation frequency in TNBC, supporting this genetic association.

genes/0.notes: TP53 mutations occur in approximately 80% of TNBC, the highest rate among breast cancer subtypes. Mutations are typically missense in the DNA-binding domain or truncating mutations.

genes/1.notes: BRCA1 germline mutations are enriched in TNBC, occurring in 10-15% of cases. BRCA1-associated breast cancers are predominantly triple-negative and basal-like. Somatic BRCA1 mutations and promoter methylation also occur.

genes/2.notes: PIK3CA mutations occur in approximately 10-20% of TNBC, particularly in the LAR subtype. May identify patients who benefit from PI3K inhibitors.

evidence.snippet: Patients with a pCR after NAT had significantly better EFS (HR = 0.31; 95% PI, 0.24-0.39), particularly for triple-negative (HR = 0.18; 95% PI, 0.10-0.31) and HER2+ (HR = 0.32; 95% PI, 0.21-0.47) disease.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis confirms that achieving pCR after neoadjuvant therapy is strongly associated with improved event-free survival, particularly for TNBC.

treatments/0.description: Standard treatment includes anthracycline and taxane-based regimens given before surgery. Pathologic complete response (pCR) rates are higher in TNBC than other subtypes and strongly predict long-term outcomes.

evidence.snippet: Among patients with early triple-negative breast cancer, the percentage with a pathological complete response was significantly higher among those who received pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy than among those who received placebo plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
evidence.explanation: KEYNOTE-522 demonstrated significantly higher pCR rates with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in early TNBC.

treatments/1.description: PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy improves outcomes in early-stage and metastatic TNBC. KEYNOTE-522 established pembrolizumab in the neoadjuvant/adjuvant setting regardless of PD-L1 status.

evidence.snippet: PARP inhibition causes synthetic lethality in breast cancers associated with germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations and is routinely used in clinical practice for metastatic breast cancer.
evidence.explanation: Review confirms PARP inhibitors cause synthetic lethality in BRCA-mutated breast cancers and are standard of care for metastatic disease.

treatments/2.description: Olaparib and talazoparib are approved for germline BRCA-mutated metastatic TNBC. They exploit synthetic lethality in HRD-positive tumors unable to repair DNA double-strand breaks.

evidence.snippet: Progression-free and overall survival were significantly longer with sacituzumab govitecan than with single-agent chemotherapy among patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence.explanation: ASCENT trial demonstrated significant PFS and OS benefit with sacituzumab govitecan versus chemotherapy in metastatic TNBC.

treatments/3.description: Antibody-drug conjugate targeting Trop-2 with an SN-38 payload. Approved for previously treated metastatic TNBC with significant survival benefit demonstrated in ASCENT trial.

evidence.snippet: BL1 and BL2 subtypes had higher expression of cell cycle and DNA damage response genes, and representative cell lines preferentially responded to cisplatin.
evidence.explanation: Basal-like TNBC subtypes with DNA damage response gene expression preferentially respond to platinum chemotherapy.

treatments/4.description: Carboplatin improves pCR rates in neoadjuvant therapy, particularly in BRCA-mutated or HRD-positive TNBC. Used in combination with taxanes.

evidence.snippet: we performed an integrated analysis of 310 VOGM proband-family exomes and 336,326 human cerebrovasculature single-cell transcriptomes
evidence.explanation: Establishes the scale and design of the analysis that identified the signalling regulators and localised them to a cell type.

evidence.snippet: Integrative genomic analysis defined developing endothelial cells as a likely spatio-temporal locus of VOGM pathophysiology.
evidence.explanation: States the conclusion this node is built on: the pathophysiology is located in developing endothelial cells, a cell type at a time, rather than in an anatomical structure.

evidence.snippet: These data suggest that genetic dysregulation of Ras signaling is an important driver of VOGM pathogenesis
evidence.explanation: Supports dysregulation rather than the incorrect claim of uniformly reduced Ras signaling.

steps/3.description: VOGM-associated variants converge on signaling programs active in developing cerebral endothelium, but their effects are not accurately described as a uniform loss of Ras signaling. RASA1 is a Ras suppressor, EPHB4 kinase-domain variants lack detectable phosphotyrosine and impair kinase-dependent control, and the PTPN11 variant reported in one proband constitutively activates Ras signaling. ACVRL1, NOTCH1, and ITGB1 implicate additional endothelial developmental pathways. Integrated exome and single-cell transcriptomic analysis places this susceptibility in developing endothelial cells.

evidence.snippet: Pathway analysis showed VOGM genes are enriched in growth-factor-regulated, tyrosine receptor kinase-associated signaling, which regulates vasculogenesis, angiogenesis, and arterio-venous specification
evidence.explanation: Links the human genetic signal to the specific developmental vascular processes represented by this node.

evidence.snippet: impaired remodeling of primitive vascular plexuses by VEGF-regulated sprouting angiogenesis, a process required for development of hierarchical arterial-capillary-venous networks
evidence.explanation: Directly identifies the developmental process disrupted by the patient-derived EPHB4 kinase-domain variant in fetal endothelial cells.

steps/4.description: Failure to remodel primitive vascular plexuses through sprouting angiogenesis disrupts the normal arterial-capillary-venous hierarchy. This separates the molecular signaling abnormality from the later anatomical lesion: the developmental process is impaired before a focal artery-to-vein connection persists.

evidence.snippet: Vein of Galen malformations (VOGMs), the most common and severe arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) of the human neonatal brain11,12, directly connect primitive choroidal or subependymal cerebral arteries to the MPV without an intervening capillary network.
evidence.explanation: Defines the arterial feeders, embryonic venous collector, and absent capillary network that distinguish the lesion.

evidence.snippet: The congenital malformation develops during weeks 6-11 of fetal development.
evidence.explanation: Gives the developmental window in which the shunt forms, which is what makes this an embryonic persistence rather than an acquired lesion.

evidence.snippet: Vein of Galen malformation (VGM) results from an aneurysmal aberration with an arteriovenous shunting of blood and is the most frequent arteriovenous malformation in infants and fetuses.
evidence.explanation: States the arteriovenous shunting that defines the lesion and its standing as the commonest such malformation in this age group.

steps/5.description: The anatomical lesion. Primitive choroidal or subependymal arteries connect directly to the median prosencephalic vein of Markowski without an intervening capillary network. The embryonic venous collector persists and dilates under high flow. The resulting low-resistance circuit produces the cardiac, arterial-steal, and venous-hypertension branches modeled downstream.

evidence.snippet: Locoregional venous hypertension associated with cerebral arteriovenous malformations is likely to lead to an epileptic seizure or neurological deficit due to vascular steal or chronic venous ischemia in all types of malformations.
evidence.explanation: States the mechanism directly rather than listing it: venous hypertension around the malformation injures brain through steal and chronic venous ischaemia. The authors hedge with "is likely to", and that hedge is left standing rather than sharpened.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: Puts hydrocephalus at roughly half of probands at diagnosis, which is what makes this arm worth modelling separately from the cardiac one.

steps/6.description: Raised pressure throughout the cerebral venous system, transmitted from the arterial side across the shunt. It impairs cerebrospinal fluid absorption and produces hydrocephalus, and contributes to the parenchymal injury that determines long-term neurological outcome.

evidence.snippet: Locoregional venous hypertension associated with cerebral arteriovenous malformations is likely to lead to an epileptic seizure or neurological deficit due to vascular steal or chronic venous ischemia in all types of malformations.
evidence.explanation: Names vascular steal explicitly as a route from the malformation to seizure and neurological deficit, which is exactly the claim this node makes. The authors' own hedge is preserved.

evidence.snippet: our case series confirms the higher risk of bleeding in AVFs related to HHT-associated variants (p = 0.034) and the risk of neurological deficit or seizure at onset (p < 0.0001)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies neurological deficit and seizure as presenting events in these shunts, giving the node a measured clinical consequence rather than an inferred one.

steps/7.description: Blood entering the low-resistance shunt is blood not delivered to brain parenchyma, producing chronic hypoperfusion of developing tissue. Together with venous hypertension this is the route to the parenchymal injury, seizures, and developmental impairment that dominate outcome in survivors of the cardiac phase.

evidence.snippet: Infants often die from high-output congestive heart failure.
evidence.explanation: States both the mechanism and that it is the usual cause of death, which is why this node rather than the neurological arm dominates neonatal management.

steps/8.description: The dominant threat to the newborn. A large fraction of cardiac output passes through the low-resistance shunt and returns rapidly to the right heart, which raises venous return, cardiac workload, and pulmonary blood flow. The heart may be structurally normal yet unable to sustain this volume demand.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: Gives 40 per cent of 114 probands at diagnosis, which supports the FREQUENT band. Note this counts the feature at diagnosis in a cohort that reached endovascular treatment, so it will understate the burden among neonates who present in extremis.

evidence.snippet: Infants often die from high-output congestive heart failure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes both the phenotype and its lethality in infancy.

steps/9.description: High-output cardiac failure presenting in the neonatal period, and the commonest cause of death. The heart is structurally normal; it is failing against a volume load imposed by a lesion in the head.

evidence.snippet: Risk of postnatal death was associated with severe neonatal cardiac failure (p=0.007) or isosystemic or suprasystemic pulmonary hypertension (p=0.014).
evidence.explanation: Directly reports pulmonary hypertension and its association with postnatal mortality in a long-term cohort.

steps/10.description: Raised pulmonary arterial pressure from sustained overcirculation, compounding the cardiac failure.

evidence.snippet: An ultrasonographic scan repeated in our institution confirmed the presence of hydrops fetalis with generalized skin edema, mild pericardial effusion and ascites.
evidence.explanation: Direct case-level evidence of hydrops in a fetus with the malformation. It establishes occurrence without supporting a population frequency.

steps/11.description: Generalized fetal edema with effusions and ascites can accompany severe high-output cardiac failure from the cerebral shunt. Evidence here is a directly observed VOGM case; no frequency is inferred from it.

evidence.snippet: The sonographic examination also revealed cardiomegaly with dilatation of all the four chambers and outflow tracts, tricuspid regurgitation and mild pericardial effusion.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents fetal cardiomegaly and chamber dilation in one VOGM case; it does not support a frequency estimate.

steps/12.description: Fetal cardiac enlargement with dilation of all four chambers and the outflow tracts, observed during high-output failure despite a structurally normal heart. The evidence is case-level, so no frequency is assigned.

evidence.snippet: The sonographic examination also revealed cardiomegaly with dilatation of all the four chambers and outflow tracts, tricuspid regurgitation and mild pericardial effusion.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents fetal tricuspid regurgitation in one VOGM case; no frequency or prognostic fraction is inferred.

steps/13.description: Fetal tricuspid regurgitation can accompany chamber dilation and high-output cardiac failure. A single directly observed case supports occurrence, not a frequency category.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: Reports hydrocephalus in 48 per cent of 114 probands at diagnosis, which is the basis for the FREQUENT band.

steps/14.description: Ventricular enlargement modelled provisionally as arising predominantly from impaired cerebrospinal fluid absorption under raised cerebral venous pressure. Obstruction by the dilated venous pouch, haemorrhage-related obstruction, and ex-vacuo enlargement after parenchymal injury remain alternative or additional explanations in an individual patient.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: Developmental delay in 54 per cent at diagnosis, the commonest single feature in the cohort, which supports the FREQUENT band.

evidence.snippet: Among survivors, 19 had a good outcome with normal schooling and 14 had a poor outcome.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies outcomes at school age, with a substantial minority of survivors doing poorly.

evidence.snippet: Long-term outcome of patients with VGAM appears to be less favourable than outcome described at the short- and medium-term, even in the absence of encephalomalacia at birth.
evidence.explanation: The clinically decisive caveat: outcomes deteriorate relative to earlier assessment, and a normal-appearing neonatal brain does not exclude it.

steps/15.description: Developmental impairment in survivors, and the outcome that matters most once the cardiac crisis is past. Long-term results are explicitly worse than medium-term follow-up suggests, and that applies even to children who had no encephalomalacia at birth, which means an initially reassuring neonatal assessment does not settle the prognosis.

evidence.snippet: our case series confirms the higher risk of bleeding in AVFs related to HHT-associated variants (p = 0.034) and the risk of neurological deficit or seizure at onset (p < 0.0001)
evidence.explanation: Reports seizure at onset as a measured presenting event with a p value, rather than as an item on a list of variables the study recorded.

evidence.snippet: Locoregional venous hypertension associated with cerebral arteriovenous malformations is likely to lead to an epileptic seizure or neurological deficit due to vascular steal or chronic venous ischemia in all types of malformations.
evidence.explanation: Connects the seizure to the mechanism this entry models, venous hypertension and steal, rather than leaving it as an unexplained association.

steps/16.description: Seizures from cortical injury, part of the neurological morbidity in survivors.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: Macrocephaly in 48 per cent of probands at diagnosis, equal with hydrocephalus and consistent with the two sharing a cause.

steps/17.description: Enlargement of the head, driven both by hydrocephalus and by the mass of the dilated venous pouch itself. It is one of the two commonest features at diagnosis and, in an infant presenting outside the neonatal cardiac window, often the finding that prompts imaging.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the source counts prominent face AND/OR scalp vasculature together at 45 per cent, while the HPO term available covers scalp veins alone. The composite proportion is therefore only upper-bound context for this term and does not justify assigning it a frequency category.

steps/18.description: Dilated, visible veins over the scalp and face, the outward sign of a venous system carrying arterialised flow at arterial pressure. It is a physical-exam clue that may accompany a cranial bruit and an enlarging head.

evidence.snippet: Salient features at diagnosis included developmental delay (54%), macrocephaly (48%), hydrocephalus (48%), prominent face and/or scalp vasculature (45%), cutaneous vascular lesions (22%), and congestive heart failure (40%).
evidence.explanation: The combined category occurred in 22% of 114 VOGM probands, supporting the OCCASIONAL band while not resolving lesion subtype.

steps/19.description: Capillary malformations, telangiectasias, or other skin vascular lesions occur in a gene-associated subset and may provide a clue to overlapping CM-AVM or HHT biology. The cohort grouped heterogeneous lesions, so the entry does not force them onto a single narrower HPO term.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, both patients had intracranial hemorrhage, progressive macrocephaly, and shunt-dependent hydrocephalus.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL: two ITGB1-variant patients, which establishes that the phenotype occurs but says nothing about how often. No frequency is asserted.

steps/20.description: Bleeding into or around the brain, the least predictable of the neurological consequences and the one that can convert a stable child into an emergency. Recorded here at low strength: it is documented in individual patients in the cited work rather than quantified across a cohort.

edges/3.description: Dysregulated signaling in fetal endothelium impairs remodeling of primitive vascular plexuses and development of the arterial-capillary-venous hierarchy.

edges/4.description: In the gene-associated subset, pleiotropic endothelial susceptibility can also manifest as capillary malformations or other cutaneous vascular lesions; the variant-specific intermediates and relationship to the focal cerebral lesion remain unresolved.

edges/5.description: Failure of angiogenesis and arteriovenous specification provides the developmental context for a direct shunt to persist, although the steps that make the human lesion focal remain unresolved.

edges/6.description: A low-resistance arteriovenous channel returns a large volume to the right heart without perfusing tissue.

edges/7.description: Arterial pressure transmitted to the venous side raises cerebral venous pressure.

edges/8.description: Flow preferentially entering the low-resistance shunt is flow not delivered to brain parenchyma.

edges/9.description: The clinical syndrome, presenting in the neonatal period.

edges/10.description: Reached through sustained pulmonary overcirculation.

edges/11.description: Severe fetal high-output cardiac failure can progress through venous congestion to generalized edema and effusions. The phenotype evidence is case-level and establishes occurrence, not frequency.

edges/12.description: Sustained fetal volume overload can produce dilation of the cardiac chambers and outflow tracts. The phenotype evidence is case-level and does not establish how often this occurs.

edges/13.description: Modelled through the chamber dilation and haemodynamic strain of fetal high-output failure. The cited case documents the finding but does not by itself establish its frequency or an invariant causal sequence.

open_questions/0.rationale: Mice carrying a patient-derived EPHB4 kinase-domain variant developed the angiogenic defect only when a second-hit allele was present. That single conditional clause reconciles inherited susceptibility alleles with a disease that often appears only once in a family. If a second event is required, the identity of that event is unknown in humans. It could be a somatic mutation confined to the developing cerebral endothelium, in which case it would be invisible to blood-derived sequencing and would explain both the non-penetrant carrier parents and the focal, single-lesion anatomy of a disease whose germline variant is present in every cell. It could equally be a second germline variant elsewhere, or a non-genetic developmental contingency. Endoluminal coil sampling has now recovered lesional endothelial cells safely enough for single-cell RNA sequencing, but the published study presents somatic and second-hit DNA analysis as future work rather than a completed result. The biological question therefore remains open while the sampling barrier has become experimentally tractable.

open_questions/1.rationale: The outcome literature states plainly that long-term results are less favourable than short- and medium-term assessment suggests, and that this holds even in the absence of encephalomalacia at birth. That combination is the interesting part: a normal-looking neonatal brain does not guarantee a normal-functioning school-age child. Several explanations are compatible with it and none is established. Chronic hypoperfusion and venous hypertension may injure developing tissue in ways that structural imaging does not show; the cognitive demands that reveal impairment may simply not exist in infancy; or residual shunting after treatment may continue to affect a brain that is still developing. Distinguishing them matters directly for what families are told at discharge and for how long children are followed.

hypotheses/0.description: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is caused by loss-of-function variants in ABCD1 on Xq28 encoding the peroxisomal membrane transporter ALDP, which imports very-long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) CoA-esters into the peroxisome for β-oxidation. Loss of ABCD1 function disables peroxisomal β-oxidation of saturated VLCFAs (C24:0, C26:0) and produces their pathological accumulation in plasma, adrenal cortex, Leydig cells, oligodendrocytes, and CNS myelin. VLCFA accumulation drives mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, microglial activation, and a neuroinflammatory cerebral demyelination program, alongside adrenocortical apoptosis producing primary adrenal insufficiency. Hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation and lentiviral gene therapy (elivaldogene autotemcel) halt cerebral disease progression in early-stage childhood cerebral ALD, corroborating the ABCD1-loss / VLCFA-accumulation / neuroinflammatory-demyelination axis as the canonical pathogenic mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Beyond ABCD1, environmental triggers and other genetic factors have been suggested as modifiers of the disease course.
evidence.explanation: A review of the modifier-gene literature concluding that the determinants of phenotype remain unidentified despite repeated searches.

evidence.snippet: there was no evidence that reduction of VLCFA levels improved or retarded visual pathway demyelination
evidence.explanation: Lowering plasma VLCFA markedly, without arresting demyelination, is direct clinical evidence that the VLCFA level is not the proximate determinant of neurological progression once disease is established.

evidence.snippet: By age 60, 76 % of males had developed adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN), 44 % had developed cerebral ALD (cALD), and 44 % had adrenal insufficiency.
evidence.explanation: A genetically ascertained national cohort quantifies the incomplete and divergent penetrance of the three arms, which is the observation the gap is about.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the central unresolved question in X-ALD and the reason the canonical model is annotated as necessary but not sufficient downstream. The genotype carries no phenotype information, so modifier genes, environmental exposure, or stochastic factors must decide conversion, and none has been identified: candidate-gene work on the CD1 locus, other ABCD paralogues, and methionine metabolism has not replicated, and no genome-wide association study has been published. The therapeutic corollary is that normalizing plasma VLCFA is not by itself sufficient, as the Lorenzo's oil visual-pathway trial showed. Without the trigger, prevention is impossible and management stays reactive MRI surveillance. Note that the conversion fraction itself is cohort- and age-dependent: reviews commonly quote 35 to 40 percent of males while the Danish national cohort reports 44 percent by age 60, so no single figure should be curated as settled.

evidence.snippet: Animal models for the disease recapitulate the biochemical signature of VLCFA accumulation and demonstrate mitochondrially generated reactive oxygen species, oxidative damage, increased glial death, and axonal damage.
evidence.explanation: Establishes what the models do capture, which is the basis for treating them as informative for the metabolic and oxidative nodes of this entry.

evidence.snippet: cerebral invasion of leukocytes and demyelination were not observed in any animal model for X-ALD, reflecting upon pathological processes that are yet to be discovered
evidence.explanation: States the mismatch directly: the cerebral lesion that defines the childhood cerebral subtype has no spontaneous model counterpart.

evidence.snippet: We generated a cALD phenotype in Abcd1-knockout mice using a 2-hit method that combines cuprizone and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models.
evidence.explanation: The cerebral phenotype had to be induced by adding demyelinating and autoimmune insults to the ABCD1 defect, which shows the gap is a missing second hit rather than a missing readout.

open_questions/1.rationale: Model evidence exists and is informative for the upstream and metabolic arms of this entry: Abcd1-null animals reproduce VLCFA accumulation, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, oxidative damage, glial death, and axonal damage, which is why they support the oxidative-stress and axonopathy nodes. What no model reproduces spontaneously is the defining lesion of the cerebral phenotype, namely leukocyte invasion of the brain with inflammatory demyelination. A cerebral phenotype can be obtained only by adding a second, artificial immune insult on the Abcd1-knockout background. Translational validity, not absence of evidence, is therefore the open question for every mechanism curated in this entry between microglial activation and demyelination, and a negative result in an Abcd1-null mouse should not be read as disproof of a human mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The pathogenesis of X-ALD related PAI is still unclear
evidence.explanation: A dedicated review of adrenal involvement in ALD states the mechanistic gap directly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

evidence.snippet: there is no evidence so far that HCT can change the course of PAI in ALD patients
evidence.explanation: Documents that the treatment which halts the cerebral arm leaves the adrenal arm untouched. Note the source frames this as absence of evidence plus absence of reported reversals, not as a demonstrated mechanistic dissociation.

evidence.snippet: In Abcd1 knockout mice, HPCD injections reduced cholesterol and VLCFA sequestration in the brain and adrenal cortex.
evidence.explanation: The first pharmacological rescue of adrenal function in an ALD model, and the only currently testable mechanistic proposal for the adrenal arm. Single study, mouse and knockdown-cell evidence only.

open_questions/2.rationale: Adrenal insufficiency is one of the most common manifestations of ALD, yet the step between VLCFA accumulation and adrenocortical failure is the least characterized part of this entry's pathograph, which currently draws a single direct edge from VLCFA accumulation to adrenocortical dysfunction with no intermediate. The clinical record shows the adrenal arm behaves differently from the cerebral arm: no reversal of established adrenal insufficiency has been reported after transplant or gene therapy, and treated patients continue lifelong glucocorticoid replacement. Whether that reflects a genuinely cell-autonomous pathway, or only irreversible cortical damage already present at treatment, is unresolved. One testable mechanism has emerged: lysosomal cholesterol trapping impairing delivery of substrate for steroidogenesis, with 2-hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin raising adrenocortical hormone levels in Abcd1-knockout mice. It rests on a single study whose cellular arm used gene knockdown rather than patient material and whose central claim is about peroxisomal disorders generally, so it is recorded here as a lead rather than as a pathograph node.

evidence.snippet: In perilesional white matter, increases in myelin peroxidation and Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 are observed.
evidence.explanation: Reports the imaging and tissue findings behind the ferroptosis proposal. A single study, framed by its authors as implicating rather than establishing the pathway.

open_questions/3.rationale: Iron accumulation, myelin peroxidation, and raised ACSL4 have been reported in perilesional white matter, which would place an iron-dependent death pathway alongside the innate and adaptive immune arms already curated here. The finding rests on one study with no intervention arm and no replication, and the authors themselves phrase the conclusion as implicating rather than demonstrating ferroptosis, so it is recorded as an emerging hypothesis rather than as a pathophysiology node. Directionality is the specific problem: perilesional tissue sits at the advancing edge of an active lesion, so the markers are equally consistent with ferroptosis driving lesion expansion and with its being a consequence of ongoing myelin breakdown.
